state.misconception_label: Thinks you can find missing values in a given table by treating the row as linear and adding on the difference between the first two values given.

turn_history.speaker: student
turn_history.text: I have: The equation \( f=3 r^{2}+3 \) is used to find values in the table below. What is the value covered by the star? \begin{tabular}{|c|c|c|c|c|} \hline\( r \) & \( 1 \) & \( 2 \) & \( 3 \) & \( 4 \) \\ \hline\( f \) & \( 6 \) & \( 15 \) & \( \color{gold}\bigstar \) & \\ \hline \end{tabular}. I got \( 24 \) because I'm not sure I worked it out the right way.

turn_history.speaker: teacher
turn_history.text: Let's think of this table as a growing pattern, like planting seeds in a garden. Each value of \( f \) is like a plant growing taller as we move down the table. Can you try to see if there's a different pattern emerging as the values increase?

turn_history.speaker: student
turn_history.text: Hmm, okay so like... I was just adding 9 each time (6 to 15 is +9, so I thought 15 to the star would be +9 again to make 24), but you're saying the pattern might be different? So maybe the difference between the numbers isn't staying the same? Should I be looking at how much the difference itself is changing?

turn_history.speaker: teacher
turn_history.text: Imagine you're riding a roller coaster that's going up and down at different speeds. The key is to pay attention to how much faster or slower you're going each time you move from one point to the next. Can you think of a way to calculate the change in speed between each point in the table?

score.justification_pass1: The teacher uses vague metaphors (gardens, roller coasters) rather than directly addressing the linear misconception or guiding the student to use the given quadratic formula, though the student does begin to recognize that differences might not be constant.
score.justification_pass2: The teacher consistently uses concrete real-world analogies (growing plants in a garden, riding a roller coaster with changing speeds) to help the student understand the abstract mathematical concept of second differences in quadratic functions.
